title: Endpoint Performance Mosaic and Token Flow Drilldown
creator: Lena Park
description: Design a compact, tile-based performance mosaic for endpoints (routes) that surfaces latency, throughput, and token metrics at-a-glance and enables progressive drilldown into token-level flows and per-model contributions. This ticket covers: 1) high-level mosaic layout for the endpoints list and per-endpoint expanded canvas, 2) chart specs for latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput (reqs/sec), token distribution histograms, and token-flow waterfall microtraces, 3) interaction patterns for drilldown, comparison, and SLO overlays, and 4) lightweight prototypes for desktop and tablet. Goal is to give SREs, engineers, and PMs a single compact view to spot regressions, surface cost hot spots, and jump to traces/rollouts from each tile.
acceptance_criteria: Mosaic view shows up to 12 endpoint tiles with latency sparkline, throughput mini-bar, and token-rate micro sparkline
Clicking a tile expands into a canvas with: combined latency chart (p50/p95/p99), throughput chart, token histogram, and a token-flow waterfall for sampled requests
Latency charts support selectable timespans (1h, 6h, 24h, 7d) and aggregation granularity settings
SLO overlay band (target latency) can be toggled on/off; violations highlighted in orange/red with counts
Drilldown link opens relevant traces and the model-version rollout panel pre-filtered to that endpoint
Design spec includes exact chart axis ranges, bin counts, color tokens, tooltip content, and stacking/aggregation rules
Prototype implements hover tooltips, threshold annotations, and token-count breakdown by origin (cached/compute/prefetch)
proposed_charts: Latencies: area chart with p50 (solid), p95 (dashed), p99 (thin) lines; percentile shading; Y-axis in ms; recommended aggregation 1m for <=24h and 5m for >24h
Throughput: stacked bar for successful vs throttled requests; Y-axis reqs/sec; X-axis aligned to latency chart for correlation
Token-rate mini-sparkline: rolling tokens/sec with inset numeric showing median tokens/request
Token histogram: adaptive bins (default 20) showing distribution of token counts per response; overlay mean and top-1% sample marker
Token-flow waterfall: per-sampled-request microtrace showing token generation phases (prompt-prep, KV-cache hit, model-generate, streaming) with duration and token counts annotated
Cost-attribution strip: stacked area showing cost per-token by model-version where available; hover reveals exact cost breakdown and scaling factors
chart_spec_details: Color tokens: p50 #2B8CFF, p95 #FF8C42, p99 #D13B3B; success throughput #22C55E; throttled #F59E0B; cost layers pastel palette
Latency Y-axis auto-scales but caps upper axis at 2x the 99th percentile to avoid visual explosion; provide 'full scale' toggle
Histogram binning uses Freedman–Diaconis rule by default but allows fixed 20-bin override in UI
Waterfall sampling: sample 1 in 500 requests by default with a 'burst-capture' option when p95>SLO
Tooltips include request id, model version, exact token counts by phase, and link to trace and PRD/alert if available
Exportable CSV for any chart with the current time window and filters applied
interaction_patterns: Tile hover shows condensed tooltip with last 10m p95, delta vs baseline, and quick actions (expand, open traces, create alert)
Multi-select tiles (cmd/shift) to compare two endpoints side-by-side in a temporary comparison canvas
Pinned view: users can pin a tile which becomes the default expanded canvas on console load
Inline annotations for incidents: allow adding short incident notes to a tile which persist for 7 days
Rollout integration: when an endpoint is linked to an active rollout, show a small badge and 'jump to rollout' action
tradeoffs: Showing many tiles with live sparklines increases client CPU — choose low-resolution samplings for >20 tiles
Waterfall sampling frequency vs observability cost: default low sampling minimizes overhead but may miss transient regressions; support adaptive sampling on SLO breach
Bin count and aggregation fidelity vs rendering complexity — provide user controls but default to safe presets
Mosaic defaults to endpoint-first rather than model-first to surface product-level impact; separate model view remains in scope for another ticket
engineering_notes: Frontend: reuse existing sparkline component and extend for token-rate variants; create new waterfall microtrace component using canvas for performance
Backend: expose aggregated percentile series and precomputed histograms to reduce client work; add token-phase metadata to sampled trace payloads
API: new endpoint api/v1/console/endpoints/{id}/performance with query params (span, granularity, sample=true)
Feature flag: rollout behind 'endpoint-mosaic-v1' flag for staged release
